tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.

- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	"""The Python surface: a constructor, two collectives, and an output allocator.
2	
3	Everything that survives a call -- the symmetric windows, the cached plans, the staging buffers --
4	lives in C++ (src/group.cc). What stays here is what has no C++ equivalent: the process group's
5	name, the comm stream, and ``AsyncCollectiveTensor``.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import warnings
11	
12	import torch
13	import torch.distributed as dist
14	import torch.distributed._symmetric_memory as symm_mem
15	from torch.distributed._functional_collectives import AsyncCollectiveTensor
16	
17	from . import _C
18	
19	
20	class CompletedHandle:
21	    """What the async call returns on a build whose libtorch has no ``c10d::register_work``. With
22	    no registry to bind the completion event to, the C++ side has already made the caller's stream
23	    wait on it, so ``wait()`` only unwraps -- a distinct type so that is visible."""
24	
25	    def __init__(self, tensor: torch.Tensor) -> None:
26	        self._tensor = tensor
27	
28	    def wait(self) -> torch.Tensor:
29	        return self._tensor
30	
31	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
32	        return f"CompletedHandle({tuple(self._tensor.shape)}, {self._tensor.dtype})"
33	
34	
35	class UlyssesGroup:
36	    """Ulysses all-to-all over NVLink, moved by the copy engines.
37	
38	    Construction is collective over ``process_group``. Windows are allocated on the first call that
39	    needs one and cached, so every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. Contract:
40	    docs/api.md.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(
44	        self,
45	        process_group: dist.ProcessGroup | None = None,
46	        device: torch.device | str | int | None = None,
47	        *,
48	        require_nvlink: bool = True,
49	    ) -> None:
50	        """
51	        Args:
52	            process_group: the group this collective runs over; ``None`` uses ``dist.group.WORLD``.
53	            device: this rank's CUDA device, as anything ``torch.device`` accepts; ``None`` and a
54	                device with no index both use the current device.
55	            require_nvlink: refuse a group whose GPUs are not all NVLink-joined. ``False`` is for
56	                measuring that case, not for running in it.
57	        """
58	        # Before anything that can throw: a refused construction -- a non-NVLink group, a device
59	        # that is not CUDA -- still leaves an object for __del__ to run on, with nothing to
60	        # release.
61	        self._destroyed = True
62	        pg = process_group if process_group is not None else dist.group.WORLD
63	        self.pg = pg
64	        self.rank = dist.get_rank(pg)
65	        self.world_size = dist.get_world_size(pg)
66	        # Normalised, because everything below indexes `device.index`: a bare "cuda:0" string has
67	        # no .index attribute, and torch.device("cuda") has one that is None. Both used to fail
68	        # several lines later, on a message about neither the device nor this constructor.
69	        device = torch.device("cuda" if device is None else device)
70	        if device.type != "cuda":
71	            raise ValueError(f"device must be a CUDA device, got {device}")
72	        if device.index is None:
73	            device = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())
74	        self.device = device
75	        torch.cuda.set_device(device)
76	
77	        if require_nvlink:
78	            self._require_nvlink()
79	
80	        # Registers the group with torch's symmetric-memory bootstrap, which rendezvous needs. It
81	        # is idempotent, and deprecated from torch 2.13 (where rendezvous resolves the group by
82	        # itself) -- calling it anyway is what keeps 2.10 working.
83	        with warnings.catch_warnings():
84	            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", FutureWarning)
85	            symm_mem.enable_symm_mem_for_group(pg.group_name)
86	
87	        self._handle = torch.classes.fast_ulysses.UlyssesGroup(
88	            pg.group_name, int(self.rank), int(self.world_size), int(device.index)
89	        )
90	
91	        # High-priority stream for the async call only; the sync call stays on the caller's stream,
92	        # since routing it through here costs two event hops. The two streams are NOT ordered
93	        # against each other, which is why the C++ side gives them separate windows.
94	        _, greatest = torch.cuda.Stream.priority_range()
95	        self._comm_stream = torch.cuda.Stream(device=device, priority=greatest)
96	        self._destroyed = False
97	
98	    def _require_nvlink(self) -> None:
99	        """Every rank checks the same set of devices, so the answer is identical on all of them and
100	        the refusal is collective in practice."""
101	        local = torch.tensor([self.device.index], dtype=torch.int64, device=self.device)
102	        gathered = [torch.zeros_like(local) for _ in range(self.world_size)]
103	        dist.all_gather(gathered, local, group=self.pg)
104	        devices = [int(t.item()) for t in gathered]
105	        if len(set(devices)) != len(devices):
106	            return  # more than one rank per GPU: not a topology this check is about
107	        problem = _C.check_nvlink(devices)
108	        if problem:
109	            raise RuntimeError(problem)
110	
111	    def all_to_all_4d(
112	        self,
113	        x: torch.Tensor,
114	        *,
115	        mode: int = 0,
116	        out: torch.Tensor | None = None,
117	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
118	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
119	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
120	        """mode 0 scatters heads and gathers sequence; mode 1 inverts it.
121	
122	        Returns a tensor the caller owns, with no lifetime rules. ``out`` from ``empty_output()``
123	        skips the copy-out; any other contiguous CUDA tensor of the output shape is copied into.
124	
125	        ``seq_splits[p]`` / ``head_splits[p]`` are rank p's sequence and head shard: pass both or
126	        neither, identical on every rank and matching the shape handed in. Neither means even
127	        shards. Collective: every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes.
128	        """
129	        if out is None:
130	            return torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d(
131	                self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits
132	            )

134	        # out-variant mutates a buffer the caller already owns, so it carries no autograd formula
135	        # and what comes back is that buffer -- backward() would run to completion and leave
136	        # x.grad as None. The returned value cannot signal it either, since nothing distinguishes
137	        # a caller who wanted no gradient from one whose gradient was dropped.
138	        if torch.is_grad_enabled() and x.requires_grad:
139	            raise RuntimeError(

141	                "op with no backward, so the gradient would be dropped without an error. Drop "
142	                "out=, or run under torch.no_grad()."
143	            )
144	        # Two ops, one method: the out-variant declares the alias it really has, which is what
145	        # keeps the functional one differentiable. See the note in src/bindings.cc.
146	        torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_out(
147	            self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits, out
148	        )

161	        """``all_to_all_4d`` on this group's comm stream, returning immediately.
162

166	        waiting.
167

170	        through four windows per dtype, so at most four lent results may be alive at once -- a
171	        fifth call raises rather than overwriting one, and the count is per rank, so every rank has
172	        to drop its results at the same point in its own program. Mutually exclusive with ``out=``.
173	        Like the rest of this method it is not differentiable.
174	
175	        Wait on, or use, every result: a dropped one leaves its entry in torch's work registry, and
176	        ``out=`` is the hole, since reading your own ``out`` never touches the registry. On a

234	    def empty_output(
235	        self,
236	        x: torch.Tensor,
237	        *,
238	        mode: int = 0,
239	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
240	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
241	    ) -> torch.Tensor:
242	        """A buffer shaped like ``all_to_all_4d(x, mode=...)``'s output, in symmetric memory.
243	
244	        Passing it back as ``out=`` makes the peers write it directly, which removes the copy-out.
245	        You own it: keep it across steps, free it when you like, and it may outlive the group.
246	        COLLECTIVE, so allocate outside the loop -- and use one buffer per concurrent call, since a
247	        call overwrites it.
248	        """
249	        return torch.ops.fast_ulysses.empty_output(self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits)

252	        self,
253	        x: torch.Tensor,
254	        *,
255	        mode: int = 0,
256	        seq_splits: list[int] | None = None,
257	        head_splits: list[int] | None = None,
258	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, float]]:
259	        """BENCHMARKS ONLY: the copying call with CUDA events between its stages, which sum to the
260	        whole call because they are strictly ordered on one stream. Reading the events syncs."""
261	        out, stages = torch.ops.fast_ulysses.all_to_all_4d_timed(
262	            self._handle, x, mode, seq_splits, head_splits
263	        )
264	        names = ("barrier_in", "transfer", "barrier_out", "copy_out")

267	    def destroy(self) -> None:
268	        """Release the group's windows and its transfer stream. Collective: dropping a window is.
269	        Buffers from ``empty_output()`` are unaffected -- they are yours."""
270	        if self._destroyed:
271	            return
272	        # Drain the comm stream first: dist.barrier only syncs the caller's current stream, so an

274	        self._comm_stream.synchronize()

281	        # The handle's C++ destructor waits on the internal transfer stream but knows nothing of
282	        # this one, so an unwaited async call could still be writing a window as it is freed.
283	        # There is no barrier here on purpose: a finalizer is no place for a collective, which is
284	        # why destroy() and not this is the supported path.

1	# API
2	
3	Shapes: `b` batch, `d` head dim, `ws` world size. `s_local` / `n_local` are this rank's sequence
4	and head shard; `s_global = sum(seq_splits)`, `n_global = sum(head_splits)`.
5	
6	## Collective contract
7	
8	Violating these hangs the group. Nothing raises and nothing times out.
9	
10	- **Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes.** A window is allocated on the first call
11	  that needs one, and that allocation is collective.
12	- **Construction, `empty_output()` and `destroy()` are collective** over `process_group`.
13	- **Every rank must issue the same sequence of dtypes**, for the same reason as shapes: a window is
14	  allocated per `(role, dtype)`.
15	- **With autograd, every rank's engine must reach the backward node in the same order.** In
16	  sequence parallelism it does, because every rank runs the same graph — but it is a new way to
17	  hang, and the graph holds the group alive, so a graph replayed after `destroy()` raises.
18	- **One buffer, one call at a time.** A call overwrites the buffer it writes into, so two
19	  concurrent calls need two `empty_output()` buffers — or `all_to_all_4d_async(lend=True)`, which
20	  keeps the buffers itself and rotates through them.
21	
22	## `UlyssesGroup(process_group=None, device=None, *, require_nvlink=True)`
23	
24	| Parameter | Meaning |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `process_group` | The group to run over; `None` uses `dist.group.WORLD`. Any subgroup works — there is no restriction on which ranks it contains. |
27	| `device` | This rank's CUDA device; `None` uses the current device. |
28	| `require_nvlink` | Refuse a group whose GPUs are not all NVLink-joined. `False` is for measuring that case, not for running in it. |
29	
30	The NVLink check reads the link type from NVML. Both a direct GPU-to-GPU link and two GPUs on one
31	NVSwitch fabric count. The check **fails open**: when NVML cannot answer — it is missing, or one
32	device cannot be probed — the group is built with no refusal and no warning, so a PCIe group on
33	such a machine runs, slowly, instead of being caught here. It is also skipped when two ranks share
34	a GPU, which is not a topology it can say anything about.
35	
36	## `fast_ulysses.nvlink_matrix(devices) -> dict[(int, int), bool] | None`
37	
38	The same probe, on its own: for a list of CUDA device indices, which ordered pairs are NVLink-joined.
39	`None` when NVML cannot answer at all. Not collective, and it takes no group — `fast-ulysses doctor`
40	prints it as a matrix.
41	
42	## `all_to_all_4d(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None) -> Tensor`
43	
44	| mode | input | output |
45	| --- | --- | --- |
46	| 0 — scatter heads, gather sequence | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` |
47	| 1 — the inverse | `(b, s_global, n_local, d)` | `(b, s_local, n_global, d)` |
48	
49	`x` is 4D CUDA, one of `float16` / `bfloat16` / `float32` / `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` /
50	`int8` / `uint8`, with `d * elem_size` 16-byte aligned; `.contiguous()` is applied internally.
51	Note the alignment rule tightens as the element shrinks: `d % 8` at float16, `d % 4` at float32,
52	`d % 16` at float8 and int8. Nothing below the check is dtype-specific — the transport moves bytes.
53	
54	**Differentiable, except with `out=`.** The vjp of a permutation is the inverse permutation, so the
55	backward is the other `mode` with the **same** splits. `all_to_all_single`'s backward swaps its
56	split sizes, because those describe one call's send and receive counts; `seq_splits` /
57	`head_splits` describe the group's geometry, which holds whichever way the data moves. Backward
58	always takes the copying path, never `out=`.
59	
60	A **meta** kernel propagates shapes under `FakeTensor` and AOTAutograd. `torch.compile` over a
61	module that holds an `UlyssesGroup` still graph-breaks: the group is a torchbind object with no
62	registered fake class. `empty_output()` refuses to be traced at all, with a message saying why.
63	
64	**Forward-mode AD works; reverse-mode `torch.func` does not.** A dual input carries its tangent
65	through a second collective, so `torch.autograd.forward_ad`, `torch.func.jvp` and
66	`torch.func.linearize` all run, at twice the traffic. `grad` / `vjp` / `jacrev` raise on their own:
67	the backward is a C++ `torch::autograd::Function`, which functorch cannot lift. `vmap` raises by an
68	explicit check on a batched input — it would run the collective once per batch element, so ranks
69	that disagree on the batch size would issue different numbers of collectives and hang. `jacfwd`
70	raises through that same check, being `vmap` over `jvp`. Map over the batch axis by reshaping it
71	into `b`, which the collective already carries.
72	
73	**`out`** decides the speed:
74	
75	- **absent, or a plain tensor of the output shape** — the transfer lands in a window this group
76	  keeps, and one flat device-to-device copy moves it out. The result is the caller's, with no
77	  lifetime rules.
78	- **a buffer from `empty_output()`** — the peers write it directly and there is no copy-out. Still
79	  the caller's own buffer, so still no lifetime rules; it is simply overwritten by the next call
80	  that uses it, like any output buffer.
81	
82	**`out` is not differentiable, and raises rather than dropping the gradient.** It reaches a
83	mutating op with no autograd formula, so the result is the buffer itself — `grad_fn` is `None`.
84	Returning that quietly would be indistinguishable from a caller who wanted no gradient, so a
85	grad-requiring input under grad mode raises instead. Use `out=` in inference or under
86	`torch.no_grad()`, where it is accepted; use the plain call inside a training graph.
87	
88	**`seq_splits[p]` / `head_splits[p]`** are rank p's sequence and head shard. Pass **both or
89	neither**, identical on every rank, matching the shape handed in. Neither means even shards, and
90	the scattered axis must then divide (`n_global % ws` for mode 0, `s_global % ws` for mode 1). Both
91	lets shards differ arbitrarily, which is what lets a caller drop sequence padding.
92	
93	### Raises
94	
95	`RuntimeError`, from validation that runs **before the call's first barrier**, so a rejected
96	argument leaves no rank waiting on peers that did not reject it: the group already `destroy()`ed;
97	`x` not 4D or not CUDA, or on a device other than the group's; dtype not in the dtype list above;
98	`d * elem_size` not 16 B-aligned; `mode` not 0 or 1; one of the splits without the other, or splits
99	contradicting `x`'s shape; no splits and the scattered axis does not divide; every rank's shard
100	empty, so the call moves no data; `out` not contiguous CUDA, on another device, or its dtype or
101	shape not the output's; `x` overlapping the window, or `out` partially overlapping it.
102	
103	`world_size` outside `[1, 8]` is refused by the constructor, so no call reaches it.
104	
105	## `all_to_all_4d_async(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None, lend=False)`
106	
107	The same call on the group's high-priority comm stream, returning immediately.
108	
109	**Not differentiable, and it refuses rather than pretending.** An `AsyncCollectiveTensor` is built
110	with `requires_grad` on the wrapper, which makes it a leaf: autograd runs above the subclass and
111	never sees the wrapped tensor's history, so a `backward()` through it would run to completion and
112	leave `x.grad` as `None`. A grad-requiring input raises instead. Use `all_to_all_4d`.
113	
114	The result is an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`: `.wait()` returns the plain tensor, and so does the **first use by any
115	aten op** — either way the caller's stream waits on the comm stream's completion event GPU-side,
116	and the host does not block. A **view op** does not wait; it re-wraps.
117	
118	**Wait on, or use, every result.** A dropped one leaves its entry in torch's work registry and its
119	CUDA event behind; torch prints a count of the survivors at exit. `out=` is the hole, since reading
120	your own `out` never touches the registry — read the returned wrapper.
121	
122	The input is staged into a persistent per-`(shape, dtype)` buffer on the caller's stream, so `x` is
123	never retained cross-stream. That costs one device copy per call. Buffers of one shape form a pool
124	of **4**, so that many same-shaped calls can be in flight before one waits for another to retire.
125	
126	### `lend=True`
127	
128	`out=`'s saving without a buffer of your own: the peers write a window the group holds, the result
129	**is** that window, and there is no copy-out. Mutually exclusive with `out=` — passing both raises.
130	Not differentiable, like the rest of this call.
131	
132	The group keeps **4 windows per dtype and takes them in order**, one per call. Which window a call
133	fills has to be the same on every rank, since the transfer addresses the peers through that window
134	and the barrier through its signal pad; a rotation driven by the call count is the same everywhere,
135	and anything read off local reference counts is not.
136	
137	So the bound is a rule, not a hint: **at most 4 lent results alive at once, and every rank must drop
138	them at the same point in its own program.** A fifth live one raises. A rank that dropped a result
139	its peers still hold does not raise — it fills a window they are not reading, which is the hang this
140	page opens with.
141	
142	Use it when a result is consumed and released within the step that issued it, which is what a
143	split q/k/v exchange does. Keep a result across steps and `empty_output()` with `out=` is the fit.
144	
145	On a libtorch with no `c10d::register_work` there is no registry to bind to, and this returns a
146	`CompletedHandle` instead: same `.wait()`, correct results, no overlap. A distinct type, so it is
147	visible.
148	
149	The sync and async calls do not share a window, so mixing them is safe.
150	
151	## `empty_output(x, *, mode=0, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None) -> Tensor`
152	
153	A buffer shaped like `all_to_all_4d(x, mode=...)`'s output, in symmetric memory. Passing it back as
154	`out=` removes the copy-out.
155	
156	**Collective**, so allocate outside the loop and reuse it. It is an ordinary tensor: keep it across
157	steps, free it when you like, and it may outlive the group.
158	
159	It is larger than it looks. Under uneven splits the window has to hold the **largest** rank's
160	output, because the peer offsets only line up while every rank allocates the same size; the tensor
161	you get is a view of that allocation's dense prefix.
162	
163	## `destroy() -> None`
164	
165	Releases the group's windows and its transfer stream. All ranks must call it together. Buffers
166	from `empty_output()` are unaffected — they are yours.
167	
168	## Environment
169	
170	Nothing is read from the environment on the collective path. On a machine whose Fabric Manager
171	cannot bind NVLink SHARP, NCCL needs `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`; that affects the `torch.distributed`
172	bootstrap, not this operator. See [install.md](install.md).

"""Are two ulysses groups that PARTITION the job correct while both are transferring?

    torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 test/distributed/subgroup.py

The layout is tp=2 x sp=ws/2, whose sp groups are the two stride-2 slices of the world -- {0,2,4,6}
and {1,3,5,7} at ws=8 -- which is the 2-D mesh docs/quickstart.md sells. Both groups run the
collective at the same time, and each rank checks its result against dist.all_to_all_single on the
MATCHING torch subgroup.

Why that is not obvious: every other worker in the suite runs on WORLD, where a group-local index
and a global one are the same number, so a build that confuses them passes all of them. Here `rank`
and `world_size` come from the subgroup (python/fast_ulysses/group.py), the peer buffer and flag
pointers come from a rendezvous keyed on the SUBGROUP's name (src/group.cc), and the barrier
publishes to `peers.p[t] + rank` with a group-local rank (src/barrier.cu). A group that rendezvoused
on the wrong name, addressed the wrong peers, or spun on the wrong flag set is a MISMATCH here
rather than a plausible answer -- and, for the ranks nobody addressed, a hang.

NEW IN v0.2, and why phase 2 is stronger than master's divergent worker: reserve()/seal() are gone,
so the collective allocation is back ON the call path. window() allocates on the first call with a
bigger shape and empty_output() allocates every time, each of them empty_strided_p2p + rendezvous +
barrier over `group_name_` alone. So "every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes" is a
per-GROUP rule, not a per-job one, and phase 2 tests what master could only test once reserve() had
taken allocation off the call path: two groups mid-allocation and mid-transfer at the same time, on
different shapes, in opposite orders.

TWO CHECKS THAT DO NOT DEPEND ON THE TIMING BITING. There is no armable in-process control for the
MEMBERSHIP property itself -- torch's get_buffer_ptrs() is group-indexed by construction, so
master's substitution has no v0.2 analogue, and a build that addresses the wrong ranks can only be
caught by the data. So the two things the data checks silently assume are checked out of band:

  * THE PAYLOAD ARM. Every comparison below is worth nothing unless no two ranks hold the same
    bytes, so that is PROVED over WORLD rather than inferred from the seed line.
  * THE EPOCH, group._handle.epoch_debug(probe, role). Two barriers run per call, so the sync
    window's epoch is exactly 4*ITERS at the end of phase 1 (that phase's first call is what
    allocates it, and allocation zeroes the pad), it advances by exactly 6 per phase-2 iteration
    after the first, and the buffer handed to out= carries exactly 2. Torn data is a SUFFICIENT
    signal that the handshake died, never a necessary one -- a run where no peer happened to be
    late comes back clean -- and on a subgroup run the epoch is additionally what says a barrier
    ran over THIS group's flag set at all. It is in turn blind to membership. Neither check is
    redundant with the other and neither may be deleted for the other's sake.

WHAT MAKES THIS RUN BLIND. Beyond the two above, the worker rests on six arrangements, and deleting
any one of them leaves a file that still prints PASS while testing nothing:

  * torch.manual_seed(1234 + rank), the GLOBAL rank. Seed by group.rank, by my_tp, or by one
    constant and the two sp groups hold IDENTICAL payloads; a result assembled from the other
    group's peers, or from this rank's tp sibling, then compares equal. It looks like boilerplate.
    The payload arm is what refuses to let it be quietly changed.
  * THE STRIDE, ranks=range(t, ws, TP). "Simplified" to contiguous halves {0,1,2,3} / {4,5,6,7},
    group 0's group-rank equals its global rank for every member, so half the job can no longer
    tell a group index from a global one -- the exact bug class being hunted.
  * PHASE 1'S WORLD BARRIER, between the reference and the call. Each rank's reference is itself a
    collective on its own sp group, so nothing else holds the two groups in phase; without it they
    drift apart and the file degenerates into correctness.py at half the world size, with no
    concurrency at all. Interference is a race; without simultaneity it is untested.
  * PHASE 2'S ABSENCE OF ONE, together with list(reversed(calls)). Both are inversions of what a
    maintainer will "fix". A barrier inside that loop, for symmetry with phase 1, re-aligns the
    groups so that neither ever allocates while the other is mid-transfer; dropping `reversed`
    makes both groups issue identical shapes at identical points, which is what phase 1 covers
    already. Either edit deletes the property with no visible change in the output.
  * PHASE 2'S ONE-SIDED SKEW. The two groups run the SAME total work per iteration -- 8, 8, 24, 24
    against 24, 24, 8, 8 -- so with nothing else in the loop the interleaving that iteration 0
    happened to produce simply repeats, and four iterations sample one arrangement rather than
    four. The GEMM chain grows with `it` to walk the phase offset, and it runs on ONE group: run
    on both it re-aligns them, exactly like the barrier that must not be there.
  * empty_output() INSIDE the phase-2 loop. It contradicts docs/api.md ("allocate outside the
    loop") and reads as a mistake; it is deliberate. window() stops allocating once it has grown to
    the largest shape in the table, so from iteration 1 on this is the only thing still putting a
    subgroup-collective rendezvous on the call path while the other group is mid-transfer.

Also blinding, in descending order of likelihood: a reference that is anything but torch's own
collective on the MATCHING sp group (a locally recomputed permutation checks the plan, not the
membership, and membership is the point); torch.equal -> allclose; one iteration instead of four,
since this is a race and not a constant; one mode; dropping the (world_size, rank) assertion; and
aggregating the failures over sp_pg instead of WORLD, which leaves rank 0's verdict covering only
its own group.

NOT COVERED, deliberately. Groups that OVERLAP rather than partition: nothing in the v0.2
constructor can hang on overlap any more (no communication library is left in C++, and its only
collective is the NVLink all_gather, over the subgroup), but the collectives moved onto the call
path, so overlapping groups reduce to the ordinary nested-collective ordering rule -- every shared
rank must enter the two groups' collectives in the same relative order, exactly as two overlapping
NCCL subgroups must. Nothing here detects a violation of it, and a worker for it would hang rather
than fail. Also not covered: the async window, whose rendezvous is a second one on the same group
name and no new membership arithmetic; and destroy()'s barrier SCOPE, since both groups tear down
together after a WORLD all_reduce, so a regression of dist.barrier(group=self.pg) to WORLD would
merely serialise here and still pass.

Below 4 ranks, or at an odd world size, there is nothing to test and this SKIPS: at sp == 1
fast_barrier returns before launching anything (src/barrier.cu) and the transfer is a self-copy, so
an unguarded run would pass while moving no data between ranks.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from correctness import reference_even  # sibling worker; torchrun puts this dir on sys.path

from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

TP = 2
B, D = 2, 128
ITERS = 4  # >= 2: phase 2's epoch check needs iterations after the one that grows the window
BALLAST = 8  # GEMMs per iteration index, on group 1 only; the phase offset between the groups


def main() -> None:
    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
    rank, ws = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", rank)))
    dev = torch.device("cuda", torch.cuda.current_device())

    # A clean exit 0, not an error: test/test_distributed.py runs every worker at nproc=3 as well
    # and asserts returncode == 0, so a machine where nothing is wrong must not fail the suite.
    if ws < 2 * TP or ws % TP:
        if rank == 0:
            print(f"SUBGROUP SKIP (needs an even world size >= {2 * TP}, got {ws})", flush=True)
        dist.destroy_process_group()
        return

    # dist.new_group is collective over WORLD, so every rank builds BOTH and keeps the one it is in:
    # sp group t = {t, t+TP, t+2*TP, ...}, stride TP -- the ulysses dimension of a tp-major mesh.
    sp_pgs = [dist.new_group(ranks=list(range(t, ws, TP))) for t in range(TP)]
    my_tp = rank % TP
    sp_pg = sp_pgs[my_tp]
    sp = ws // TP

    group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_pg, require_nvlink=False)

    # Named here rather than left to surface as a wrong answer later. Aggregated over WORLD before
    # anyone acts on it, because a build that gets this wrong on SOME ranks would otherwise leave
    # the rest waiting in a barrier for a peer that had already exited -- a hang, not a failure.
    ok = int((group.world_size, group.rank) == (sp, rank // TP))
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"FAIL rank={rank}: group is ({group.world_size}, {group.rank}), expected "
            f"({sp}, {rank // TP}) -- derived from WORLD rather than from process_group",
            flush=True,
        )
    agree = torch.tensor([ok], device=dev)
    dist.all_reduce(agree)
    if int(agree.item()) != ws:
        # Identical on every rank, so every rank leaves here and none is left waiting.
        dist.destroy_process_group()
        raise SystemExit(1)

    # The GLOBAL rank, so every rank's payload is unique. This is the negative control: seeded by
    # anything group-local, the two sp groups hold identical data and a result assembled from the
    # wrong peers compares equal. See the docstring.
    torch.manual_seed(1234 + rank)
    failed = 0

    # ARM IT. Drawn from the same generator as every payload below and gathered over WORLD, since
    # the collision that matters is between the two sp groups: if this passes, no comparison in
    # this file can be satisfied by another rank's bytes. If the seed above is ever made
    # group-local, this fires instead of the whole file going quietly green.
    probe = torch.randn(64, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    drawn = [torch.empty_like(probe) for _ in range(ws)]
    dist.all_gather(drawn, probe)
    collisions = [(a, b) for a in range(ws) for b in range(a) if torch.equal(drawn[a], drawn[b])]
    if collisions:
        failed += 1
        print(
            f"FAIL rank={rank}: ranks {collisions} drew IDENTICAL payloads, so every check in this "
            "file would also be satisfied by the wrong group's data -- the seed is not per-rank",
            flush=True,
        )
    dist.barrier()

    # Not from empty_output(), so epoch() falls through owned_ to windows_[(role, dtype)] and reads
    # the INTERNAL sync window -- the one the copying calls use. bfloat16, which keys it.
    win_probe = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)

    # --- phase 1: identical shapes, maximal simultaneity ------------------------------------
    for it in range(ITERS):  # repeated: interference between the groups is a race, not a constant
        for mode in (0, 1):
            shape = (B, 16, 4 * sp, D) if mode == 0 else (B, 16 * sp, 4, D)
            x = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
            ref = reference_even(x, mode, sp, sp_pg)
            # WORLD: releases both sp groups into their a2a together. It is the only thing holding
            # them in phase -- the reference above is a collective on one sp group alone.
            dist.barrier()
            if not torch.equal(group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=mode), ref):
                failed += 1
                print(f"FAIL rank={rank} sp_group={my_tp} phase1 it={it} mode={mode}", flush=True)
    dist.barrier()

    # Both modes carry the same window_numel (b*sp*16*4*D either way), so phase 1 allocates the
    # sync window on its first call -- which zeroes the pad -- and never grows it again. The epoch
    # is therefore an absolute here, not a delta: 2 barriers x 2 modes x ITERS calls.
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    e_p1 = group._handle.epoch_debug(win_probe, 0)
    if e_p1 != 4 * ITERS:
        failed += 1
        print(
            f"FAIL rank={rank} sp_group={my_tp}: the sync window's epoch is {e_p1} after phase 1, "
            f"expected {4 * ITERS} -- this group's barrier did not run over its own flag set once "
            "per call, whether or not anything happened to tear",
            flush=True,
        )

    # --- phase 2: different shapes, in opposite orders ---------------------------------------
    calls = [(0, 8), (1, 8), (0, 24), (1, 24)]
    # Group 0 runs the table forwards, group 1 backwards, so the two groups are on different shapes
    # at every step -- and, while the windows are still growing, allocating different ones.
    mine = calls if my_tp == 0 else list(reversed(calls))
    # Allocated on every rank so the two groups stay at the same point in their generators; only
    # group 1 ever multiplies it. Saturates to inf after a few products -- nothing reads it.
    skew = torch.randn(1024, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    e_p2_start = 0  # sampled at the end of iteration 0, by which point both windows are at max

    for it in range(ITERS):
        # ONE-SIDED, and growing with `it`: the two groups' iterations cost the same, so a fixed
        # offset would replay one interleaving ITERS times. On both groups this would be a barrier
        # by another name.
        if my_tp == 1:
            for _ in range(BALLAST * it):
                skew = skew @ skew.T * 0.001
        for j, (mode, s_local) in enumerate(mine):
            shape = (B, s_local, 4 * sp, D) if mode == 0 else (B, s_local * sp, 4, D)
            x = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
            # Collective on sp_pg alone, which is why it does not re-align the two groups. And NO
            # barrier anywhere in this loop: one would re-align them, and their divergence is the
            # property being tested.
            ref = reference_even(x, mode, sp, sp_pg)
            if j == my_tp:
                # Inside the loop ON PURPOSE, against docs/api.md's advice. window() stops
                # allocating once it has grown to the largest shape in the table, so from iteration
                # 1 on empty_output() is the only subgroup-collective rendezvous left on the call
                # path while the other group is mid-transfer. Keying it on j == my_tp puts the two
                # groups' allocations at different steps and on different shapes.
                buf = group.empty_output(x, mode=mode)
                ours = group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=mode, out=buf)
            else:
                ours = group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=mode)
            if not torch.equal(ours, ref):
                failed += 1
                print(
                    f"FAIL rank={rank} sp_group={my_tp} phase2 it={it} mode={mode} s={s_local}",
                    flush=True,
                )
        if it == 0:
            # s=24 is the largest shape in the table and both groups reach it in iteration 0, so
            # the sync window is reallocated -- and its epoch reset -- somewhere inside this
            # iteration, at a step that differs per group. Everything after it is a clean delta.
            # A host read costs nothing here: torch.equal above already syncs on every call.
            torch.cuda.synchronize()
            e_p2_start = group._handle.epoch_debug(win_probe, 0)

    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    # Three of the four calls per iteration take the internal window; the fourth is zero-copy into
    # this iteration's own empty_output() buffer and touches that buffer's flags instead.
    e_p2 = group._handle.epoch_debug(win_probe, 0) - e_p2_start
    if e_p2 != 6 * (ITERS - 1):
        failed += 1
        print(
            f"FAIL rank={rank} sp_group={my_tp}: the sync window's epoch moved {e_p2} over the "
            f"last {ITERS - 1} phase-2 iterations, expected {6 * (ITERS - 1)}",
            flush=True,
        )

    # one call. Anything but 2 means the peers were not barriering on the buffer they wrote --

# Quick start

## Wrapping attention

The two calls bracket attention: mode 0 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, mode 1 trades
it back.

```python
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

dist.init_process_group("nccl")
torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
ws = dist.get_world_size()

group = UlyssesGroup()          # collective; refuses a group that is not NVLink-joined

def attention_block(qkv):       # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
    qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)      # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
    out = attention(qkv)                        # each rank now holds whole sequences
    return group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)     # -> (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
```

Pack q, k and v into one collective when you can: the last dim is just `3 * head_dim`, and one
call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three.

## Removing the copy-out

The default returns a tensor the call allocated, which costs one flat device-to-device copy out of
the window. Give it a symmetric buffer instead and the peers write that buffer directly:

```python
buf = group.empty_output(qkv, mode=0)     # collective: allocate ONCE, outside the loop
for step in range(steps):
    y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, out=buf)   # no copy-out; y is buf
```

`buf` is an ordinary tensor you own. It is overwritten by the next call that uses it, so use one
buffer per concurrent call.

`out=` gives up the gradient: the result comes back with no `grad_fn` and no `requires_grad`, and
nothing raises. Use it in inference and under `torch.no_grad()`; inside a training graph, call
without `out=`.

## Overlapping with compute

The transfer uses no SMs, so it can run underneath compute. Submit it, do the compute, then use the
result — the first aten op on it inserts the wait GPU-side.

```python
y = group.all_to_all_4d_async(qkv, mode=0)   # inference only: raises if qkv requires grad
h = some_gemm_chain(other_input)             # runs while the copy engines move qkv
y = y.wait()                                 # or just use y; the first op waits by itself
```

The async form is not differentiable and refuses a grad-requiring input rather than dropping the
gradient, so in a training step this is the sync call's job.

Wait on, or use, every async result. A dropped one leaves an entry in torch's work registry.

## Dropping the sequence padding

Sharding a sequence usually means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size and padding the
tail, so every rank holds the same length. Those padded tokens then ride through attention and the
collective on every layer of every step. Pass the real per-rank lengths instead:

```python
s = 75827                                    # does not divide by ws
seq_splits = [s // ws + (1 if p < s % ws else 0) for p in range(ws)]
head_splits = [n_global // ws] * ws

y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, seq_splits=seq_splits, head_splits=head_splits)
```

Both lists or neither, identical on every rank. Uneven is the general path here, not a slow one.

## Under 2-D parallelism

`process_group` takes any subgroup — the sp slice of a tp × sp mesh, with no restriction on which
ranks it contains:

```python
sp_group = mesh["sp"].get_group()
group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)
```

## What will hang you

Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. The first call with a new shape allocates a
window, and that allocation is collective — if one rank takes a branch the others do not, it waits
there. This is the same discipline `torch.distributed` collectives already require.

## Coming from another Ulysses

`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention` and `LongContextAttention` are attention modules, and
sglang's `usp.py` is called from one; this is only the collective, so a port replaces the module
with the two calls above plus your own attention. `scatter_idx` / `gather_idx` map to `mode`, the
`torch.autograd.Function` wrapper is deleted rather than translated, and a caller on `(s, b, n, d)`
still owes a transpose. Call by call: [migration.md](migration.md).

## Checking the machine

```bash
fast-ulysses doctor
```

Prints the build, the devices, and the pairwise NVLink matrix. A group spanning a pair marked `N`
is refused at construction.

# u2-l1 UlyssesGroup 构造与 NVLink 检查

## 1. 本讲目标

上一单元我们跑通了安装和第一次调用,本讲把镜头对准一切调用的起点——`UlyssesGroup` 的构造。读完本讲,你应该能够:

1. 说出三个构造参数 `process_group` / `device` / `require_nvlink` 各自的语义、默认值,以及它们为什么这样设计。
2. 解释**构造为什么是集合操作**(collective):NVLink 检查里的 `all_gather`、对称内存 bootstrap 注册、以及随后第一次窗口分配的 rendezvous,都要求所有成员 rank 一起到场。
3. 描述 NVLink 检查的完整链路:Python 侧收集设备号 → C++ 侧用 NVML 探测拓扑 → 拓扑不对时拒绝;以及它的**失败开放**(fail-open)语义——NVML 答不上来时放行,而不是误拒。
4. 理解**任意子组**都能用:rank / world_size 是组内编号,对称内存 rendezvous 按子组名字寻址,两个 rank 共享一块 GPU 时检查自动跳过。

## 2. 前置知识

- **进程组(process group)与 SPMD**:torchrun 启动的每个进程叫一个 rank,`dist.init_process_group("nccl")` 之后,所有 rank 默认组成 `WORLD` 组。SPMD 指每个 rank 跑同一份程序、发出同样的调用序列——这是 u1-l2 建立的契约。`dist.new_group(ranks=[...])` 可以在 `WORLD` 里再切出一个子组。
- **集合操作(collective)**:需要组内所有 rank 一起进入、缺一个就全员卡住的操作,比如 `all_gather`、`barrier`。本讲会反复遇到「某个步骤为什么必须是集合的」这个问题。
- **对称内存(symmetric memory)**:torch 提供的一种分配方式,组内每个 rank 各拿一块同尺寸缓冲,并且**互相知道对方的地址**,于是 rank A 可以直接写 rank B 的内存(通过 NVLink)。这是 fast-ulysses 传输的物理基础,细节在 u4 展开;本讲只需要知道「分配对称内存需要一次组内地址交换,叫 rendezvous」。
- **NVML**:NVIDIA Management Library,显卡管理和监控的用户态库(`libnvidia-ml.so.1`),`nvidia-smi` 背后就是它。它是唯一能查到 **NVLink 链路类型**的接口。CUDA 自己的 `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer` 只能告诉你 P2P 可用与否,PCIe 上它也返回可用,区分不了「快得值得用」和「慢得不如不用」。
- **torchbind 自定义类**:用 `TORCH_LIBRARY(...).class_<...>(...)` 注册、在 Python 侧通过 `torch.classes.命名空间.类名` 访问的 C++ 对象。`UlyssesGroup` 的全部有状态部分(窗口、plan 缓存、暂存池)都住在 C++ 对象里,Python 类只是个壳。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| [python/fast_ulysses/group.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py) | Python 门面。`UlyssesGroup.__init__`(构造参数解析、NVLink 检查、对称内存注册)、`_require_nvlink`、`destroy`。 |
| [src/nvlink.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/nvlink.cc) | NVML 探测的全部实现:`dlopen` 加载 NVML、BDF 匹配设备、直连/NVSwitch 两种拓扑、`check_nvlink` 的失败开放。 |
| [include/fast_ulysses/nvlink.hpp](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/include/fast_ulysses/nvlink.hpp) | nvlink 模块的契约注释:为什么用 NVML 而不是 `cudaDeviceCanAccessPeer`、`nullopt` 的含义。 |
| [src/group.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc) | C++ 侧 `UlyssesGroup` 构造(`world_size ∈ [1,8]` 检查)与 `allocate()`(对称内存分配 + rendezvous,本讲只看轮廓,u4 精读)。 |
| [src/bindings.cc](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc) | torchbind 类注册与 `check_nvlink` / `nvlink_matrix` 的 pybind 绑定。 |
| [docs/api.md](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md) | 集合契约与构造函数的官方文档,本讲大量论断的出处。 |
| [test/distributed/subgroup.py](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/test/distributed/subgroup.py) | 子组场景的真实测试,综合实践照着它写。 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 构造参数:process_group / device / require_nvlink

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`UlyssesGroup` 的构造函数只有三个参数,但每个都对应一个真实的设计决策:

| 参数 | 默认值 | 语义 | 设计动机 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `process_group` | `None` → `dist.group.WORLD` | 这组集合通信跑在哪个进程组上 | 支持 tp × sp 二维并行:sp 维度只是 `WORLD` 的一个切片,传子组即可,对子组包含哪些 rank 没有任何限制 |
| `device` | `None` → 当前设备 | 本 rank 用的 CUDA 设备,接受 `torch.device` / 字符串 / 整数 | torchrun 场景里每个进程按 `LOCAL_RANK` 绑好自己的卡,「当前设备」就是正确答案,所以默认值够用 |
| `require_nvlink` | `True`(仅关键字参数) | 组内 GPU 不是全互 NVLink 时拒绝构造 | 传输直接写对端内存,走 PCIe 反而比 `torch.distributed` 还慢——错误拓扑是「正确但慢」,早失败比默默慢好 |

注意 `require_nvlink` 在签名里位于 `*` 之后,是**只能关键字传参**的,这是对「它不常用、别误传」的提示。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

`__init__` 按严格顺序做八件事,顺序本身就是设计:

```text
1. self._destroyed = True     # 先立"墓碑":任何一步抛异常,__del__ 都能安全运行
2. 解析 process_group         # None → dist.group.WORLD;取组内 rank / world_size
3. 归一化 device              # str/int/None → torch.device("cuda", index)
                              # 非 CUDA → ValueError;无 index → 用当前设备
4. torch.cuda.set_device      # 把进程的当前设备钉在这块卡上
5. require_nvlink=True 时     # _require_nvlink():可能 raise(见 4.3)
6. enable_symm_mem_for_group  # 对称内存 bootstrap 注册(见 4.2)
7. 创建 C++ torchbind 句柄    # 触发 C++ 侧 world_size ∈ [1,8] 检查
8. 创建高优先级 comm 流       # 异步调用专用;最后才把 _destroyed 置 False
```

两个值得停下来想的顺序问题:

- **墓碑先行**:如果第 5 步的 NVLink 检查 raise 了,Python 对象仍然会被创建(只是 `__init__` 没跑完),`__del__` 仍会执行。`_destroyed = True` 放在最前面,保证这个半成品对象在析构时什么都不释放——此时也没有任何东西可释放。
- **NVLink 检查先于对称内存注册**:被拒绝的构造不会在 torch 的对称内存 bootstrap 里留下任何状态,失败是干净的。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

构造签名与三个参数的文档:[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L43-L57](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L43-L57)。docstring 里对 `require_nvlink` 的措辞值得记住:"`False` is for measuring that case, not for running in it"——关掉检查的唯一正当理由是测量退化,不是在 PCIe 机器上跑生产。

墓碑、进程组与设备归一化:[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L58-L75](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L58-L75)。设备归一化的注释解释了历史上踩过的坑:裸字符串 `"cuda:0"` 没有 `.index` 属性,`torch.device("cuda")` 的 `.index` 是 `None`,两者都会在几行之后炸出一个跟设备毫无关系的错误,所以这里统一收敛成带 index 的 `torch.device`。`rank` 和 `world_size` 用 `dist.get_rank(pg)` / `dist.get_world_size(pg)` 取——**是组内编号,不是全局编号**,这一点在 4.4 会变成主题。

对称内存注册与 C++ 句柄创建:[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L80-L89](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L80-L89)。注册用的 key 是 `pg.group_name`——进程组的**名字**字符串,后面所有 rendezvous 都用它寻址。C++ 句柄就是 `torch.classes.fast_ulysses.UlyssesGroup(...)`,它的注册在 [src/bindings.cc:L680-L681](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/bindings.cc#L680-L681),构造函数本体在 [src/group.cc:L145-L155](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L145-L155):只做两个 `TORCH_CHECK`——`world_size ∈ [1, 8]`(fast-ulysses 是单机库)和 `rank` 在范围内。docs/api.md 对应的一句话是「`world_size` outside `[1, 8]` is refused by the constructor, so no call reaches it」([docs/api.md:L103](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L103))。

最后是 comm 流:[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L91-L96](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L91-L96)。取 `priority_range()` 的最大优先级(数值最小)建一条新流,**只有异步调用用它**;同步调用留在调用者自己的流上,因为绕道 comm 流要多付两次事件同步。注释还预告了一个 u7 的话题:这两条流之间没有顺序关系,所以 C++ 侧给它们**分开的窗口**。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**:验证三个参数的归一化行为与失败路径,不依赖多卡。

**操作步骤**(示例代码,非项目文件):

```python
# u2_l1_params.py —— 运行: python u2_l1_params.py(需要已 init 的进程组,见步骤 3)
import os
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

dist.init_process_group("nccl")            # 构造的前提:进程组已初始化
torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", 0)))

g1 = UlyssesGroup()                        # device=None → 当前设备
g2 = UlyssesGroup(device="cuda")           # 字符串,无 index → 仍解析到当前设备
g3 = UlyssesGroup(device=torch.cuda.current_device())  # 整数索引

for g in (g3, g2, g1):
    g.destroy()

    UlyssesGroup(device="cpu")
except ValueError as e:
    print("caught:", e)                    # 预期: device must be a CUDA device, got cpu
```

**需要观察的现象**:
1. 三种 `device` 写法解析到同一个 `torch.device`。
2. `device="cpu"` 抛 `ValueError`,消息明确点名设备。

**预期结果**:归一化逻辑([group.py:L69-L74](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L69-L74))保证 1;`ValueError` 分支([group.py:L70-L71](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L70-L71))保证 2。实际运行输出待本地验证(本讲义写作环境无 GPU)。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**:为什么 `_destroyed = True` 要放在 `__init__` 的第一行,而不是在结尾和 `_destroyed = False` 配对出现的地方顺便处理?

**答案**:构造中途可能 raise(NVLink 拒绝、非 CUDA 设备)。Python 对一个 `__init__` 抛异常的对象仍会执行 `__del__`;若 `_destroyed` 属性不存在,`__del__` 会抛 `AttributeError` 并掩盖原异常。第一行先声明「无资源可释放」,让任何失败路径的析构都是安全的([group.py:L58-L61](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L58-L61) 的注释原文:"a refused construction ... still leaves an object for `__del__` to run on, with nothing to release")。

**练习 2**:`world_size = 9` 的组会在哪里、以什么形式失败?

**答案**:在 C++ 构造函数里,`TORCH_CHECK(world_size_ >= 1 && world_size_ <= 8, ...)`([src/group.cc:L151-L153](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L151-L153))。`TORCH_CHECK` 抛 `c10::Error`,到 Python 侧是 `RuntimeError`,消息为 "world_size must be in [1, 8] -- fast-ulysses is single-node -- got 9"。因为构造参数 `rank` / `world_size` 是 Python 侧从 `pg` 算好再传进去的([group.py:L87-L89](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L87-L89)),这个检查实际卡住的是「传了一个 9 rank 子组」的场景。

**练习 3**:`require_nvlink` 为什么做成仅关键字参数?

**答案**:它是个不常用的开关,且语义(关掉一个安全检查)容易被误用。放在 `*` 之后强制调用方写出 `require_nvlink=False` 这个显式动作,避免位置参数误传,也让代码审查时这行一眼可见。

### 4.2 对称内存注册:构造为何是集合操作

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

docs/api.md 的集合契约开宗明义:**"Construction, `empty_output()` and `destroy()` are collective"**([docs/api.md:L6-L20](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/docs/api.md#L6-L20))。违反集合契约的后果不是报错而是**挂起**——某个 rank 在集合点等一个永远不来的伙伴。

但「构造是集合的」这句话要拆开看,构造函数里其实有三种不同性质的步骤:

1. **真集合通信**:`_require_nvlink` 里的 `dist.all_gather`(见 4.3)——这是一次真正的组内通信,构造路径上唯一的分布式原语。
2. **本地但必须人人执行的注册**:`symm_mem.enable_symm_mem_for_group(pg.group_name)`。它是进程本地的、幂等的注册,但任何一个 rank 漏掉它,这个 rank 后续的对称内存 rendezvous 就找不到组织。
3. **纯本地构造**:C++ 句柄创建、comm 流创建——不通信,但它们的状态(rank、world_size、device)必须全组一致,而这份一致性由「同一份 SPMD 程序」保证。

此外要澄清一个容易误解的点:**构造本身并不分配对称内存窗口**。窗口是惰性的,第一次需要它的调用才分配([group.py:L38-L40](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L38-L40) 的类 docstring:"Windows are allocated on the first call that needs one and cached")。构造的「集合性」是在为那第一次分配**铺路**:每个 rank 都注册了,rendezvous 才能凑齐。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```text
构造(每个 rank 各自执行,但输入相同)
  ├─ all_gather 收集全组设备号          ← 真集合通信
  ├─ enable_symm_mem_for_group(name)    ← 本地注册,幂等,人人必须做
  └─ 创建 C++ 句柄 + comm 流            ← 本地

第一次 all_to_all_4d 调用(更严格的集合点)
  └─ allocate():
       ├─ empty_strided_p2p(...)        ← 每个 rank 分配自己的对称缓冲
       ├─ rendezvous(t, group_name)     ← 组内交换地址,必须全员到场
       ├─ 收集 peer_ptrs / flag_ptrs    ← 之后本 rank 就能直写对端
       └─ 清零自己的握手区 + barrier     ← 保证 epoch 从 0 开始
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

注册调用:[python/fast_ulysses/group.py:L80-L85](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/python/fast_ulysses/group.py#L80-L85)。注释说了两个关键事实:注册是**幂等**的;从 torch 2.13 起这个 API 已弃用(rendezvous 会自己解析进程组),但为了兼容 torch 2.10 仍然要调——所以外面套了 `catch_warnings` 压掉 `FutureWarning`。

`allocate()` 的 rendezvous 部分(轮廓,u4 精读):[src/group.cc:L218-L227](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L218-L227)。`empty_strided_p2p` 分配,`rendezvous(t, group_name_)` 按**进程组名字**完成组内地址交换;`TORCH_CHECK(sym, ...)` 的报错消息把两种失败并列出来——"The allocation is not a symmetric one, or the group is not registered with torch's symmetric-memory bootstrap"——第二种正是「某个 rank 忘了构造」的症状。

rendezvous 之后的成员资格交叉验证:[src/group.cc:L232-L244](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L232-L244)。`get_buffer_ptrs()` 返回的指针列表**按构造时的组内 rank 排列**,这里检查它的长度恰好等于 `world_size_`,否则报 "the process group and this group disagree about their membership"——这是「Python 侧的 rank/world_size 与 rendezvous 实际凑齐的成员不一致」的显式防线。最后 [src/group.cc:L250-L251](https://github.com/triple-mu/fast-ulysses/blob/ad1a4a06a42d8129a278f010b1d67a6e206d38e6/src/group.cc#L250-L251) 清零自己的握手区并 `sym->barrier(0, 0)`,保证全组的 epoch 计数器统一从零开始。

#### 4.2.4 代码实践

**实践目标**:在源码层面数清构造路径上的集合点,并理解漏掉一个 rank 的后果。

**操作步骤**(源码阅读型实践,不需要 GPU):

3. 纸面推演:ws=4,rank 2 因为一个只在自己分支里的 `if` 跳过了 `UlyssesGroup(...)` 构造,但其余三个 rank 继续发起第一次 `all_to_all_4d`。写出每个 rank 各自卡在哪里。
